title: Stranded-variant recovery & tenant communication protocol for cross-environment canary regressions
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: codify an operational protocol and runbook for 'stranded variant' scenarios where a model variant or model rollout produces a canary-quality regression affecting a subset of tenants across Hosted, Dedicated and Private planes. This ticket captures detection, containment, tenant-aware rollback choreography, KV cache reconciliation, and coordinated customer communications. Background: a recent test exchange (incidents in Feb/Mar) surfaced a failure mode where a variant swap left a non-zero set of tenants routed to an incompatible cache state (KV mismatch), causing silent degradation with high P50 latency and hallucination regressions for select customers. This ticket defines recovery steps, ownership matrix, automation gaps, recommended immediate mitigations, and postmortem follow-ups (tests, telemetry, and deployment guardrails).

acceptance_criteria: A documented runbook for stranded-variant recovery covering Hosted, Dedicated, and Private with step-by-step commands and owners
Automated KV-drift detection alert emits with actionable metadata (tenant id, variant id, timestamp)
A safe rollback choreography tested in staging that includes tenant-aware pinning and cache reconciliation without global downtime
Customer communication templates and escalation handoff checklist are approved by Support and Field Engineering
A postmortem checklist and automation backlog items created for preventing recurrence
mitigation_playbook: 1) Triage: Confirm alert signals (kv-drift.variant, canary-quality-drop.chat, p50-latency-rise) and map impacted tenant slices using trace IDs and route metadata
2) Stakeholders: Notify SRE, Runtime Eng (assignee), Support, Solutions Eng, and PM. Open incident channel #inc-variant-stranded-<date>

3) Short-term containment (Hosted): Shift affected traffic to the previous stable variant with traffic split 80/20 then 95/5. Use routing API: POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/routing/reassign with body {tenant,from_variant,to_variant,percentage}

4) Short-term containment (Dedicated): For affected Dedicated pools, mark tenant slice 'frozen' and create a warmup job to rehydrate KV on the target variant before incrementally switching traffic. Warmup script: ops/warmup/warm_kv_repopulate.sh (PR #8241)

5) Short-term containment (Private/on-prem): Coordinate with customer infra lead. Provide quick rollback package (rpm/deb) and a minimal config to pin variant via the private control plane. Escalate to account's CSM and legal if required for emergency access

6) KV reconciliation: Run per-tenant KV-diff tool: ops/tools/kv_diff --tenant <id> --from <old_variant> --to <new_variant>. If diff > threshold, run staged rehydrate then validate synthetic prompt set
7) Monitoring: Ensure end-to-end evals (regression prompt set) succeed for each tenant slice before final traffic cutover
8) Communication: Publish templated customer advisory and one-off field messages. Use templates in docs/comm_templates/variant_regression.md
9) Rollback confirmation: When rollback completes, confirm absence of residual KV entries by checking kv-drift audit log and inform Support to close customer tickets
10) Post-incident: Run a postmortem, schedule automation stories for blocking the exact failure point (e.g., automatic cache eviction on variant swap)
followups: Add automated safe-rollback guard that verifies KV parity before committing 100% traffic (story ENG-455002)
Add tenant-facing view in Console that shows variant history and KV parity state (PM-5224)
Create e2e regression test harness that simulates variant swap and verifies synthetic evals (ENG-455003)
